A kernel vector supported on the initially white set vanishes at each successive forced vertex by the equation at the black forcing vertex, so success implies independent columns. This also bounds success by six white vertices when the full rank is six. Greedy sequential tests are valid: a legal target is either already removed by other steps or still legal when the black set grows, and a stalled nonempty white set is a fort that cannot be eliminated by a different order. Independently, in the binary group algebra on four commuting involutions g_i put t_i=1+g_i, so t_i^2=0. Multiplication by 1+sum(g_i)+product(g_i) is multiplication by e_2(t)+e_3(t)+e_4(t), with e_j elementary squarefree sums. Its degree-2 image is one-dimensional; the degree-3 leading images of the four t_i have matrix J+I indexed by missing coordinate, invertible over GF(2); and a degree-2 monomial yields the full degree-4 monomial. Hence the rank is six. The 160 induced three-vertex paths arise from choosing a center and two out of five directions. For the center 0 and ends 1,2, only 7,11,12 are common nonneighbors outside the path; they are independent, and the resulting six-set is a fort. Permuting directions and translating proves transitivity; the stabilizer of 0 in the full graph automorphism group acts faithfully on the five directions since each other vertex is identified by its distinct pair of neighbors among those directions. Thus the full group is the affine group of order 1920.
